Software and environment Use the Tapirs metabarcoding workflow ( https://github.com/EvoHull/Tapirs ), which runs via Snakemake within a conda virtual environment to ensure reproducibility and software compatibility. Perform all steps on a high-performance computing cluster or equivalent local system with sufficient memory and processing power to handle demultiplexed FASTQ files.

Soil and Scat Sample Extraction Weigh out 2.5 g of sample a 10 mL Teflon grinding jars Add 5.5 mL lysis solution Add one 20 mm steel ball Homogenise using the TissueLyser II (Qiagen) according to Mu-DNA protocol settings (30 hz for 10 mins) Pour the homogenised sample lysate into a 5ml screw-cap Axygen tube (without garnet beads). At this point, samples can be frozen for later extraction if necessary Following all samples being homogenised, create a blank by adding just 5.5ml of lysis solution to the grinding jars Proceed using the Mu-DNA soil protocol after lysis. Demultiplexing Allow Illumina MiSeq Reporter software to automatically demultiplex raw sequence data into forward and reverse FASTQ files for each library Further demultiplex reads to sample level using a custom Python script that matches unique MID tag combinations from the first and second PCR rounds.

Step 1: Primer Selection and first PCR (PCR1) Use vertebrate-specific primers 12S-V5-F (5’-ACTGGGATTAGATACCCC-3’) and 12S-V5-R (5’-TAGAACAGGCTCCTCTAG-3’) (Kelly et al. 2014; Riaz et al. 2011) modified to include: Illumina sequencing adapters MID tags (8-nucleotide multiplex identifiers) - Kitson et al. 2019 Heterogeneity spacers 2. Prepare PCR1 reactions in triplicate for each sample: 12.5 µL Q5‱ Master Mix (for water/tree roller samples) or MyTaq‱ Red Mix (for soil/scat) 0.5 µL BSA (Thermo Scientific) 7 µL molecular-grade water 1.5 µL of each 10 µM tagged primer 2 µL template DNA 3. Run PCR1 on the thermal cycler with the following conditions: 98°C for 5 mins 35 cycles of 98°C for 10s, 58°C for 20s and 72°C for 30s 72°C for 7 minutes Held at 4°C 4. Include the following controls in each 24-sample sub-library At least 1 extraction blank Associated field blanks 1 negative PCR control 1 positive control: Astatotilapia calliptera DNA (0.05 ng/μL) — a tropical species not present in Scotland

steps.title: Prevent Contamination
steps.instruction: Implement strict sterilization and contamination control measures for all sampling activities.

substeps.instruction: Wear sterile gloves for each sample and change them between samples.
Wipe all collection equipment and work surfaces between samples with 10% bleach solution, followed by 70% ethanol.
For lab-based equipment or end-of-day sterilization, soak for 20 minutes in 10% bleach, 5 minutes in 5% lipsol, and rinse with distilled water.
Take a field blank (sterile water) into the field each day and process it alongside samples.
If using a single sterilized cool bag, double-bag each sample and separate them by type (e.g., water, tree roller) and habitat to prevent cross-contamination.

steps.title: Collect Water Samples
steps.instruction: Collect water samples from small water bodies such as rivers, streams, drainage channels, or puddles.

substeps.instruction: Collect ~1 L of water using Whirl-Pak® bags directly from the source; use a sterile beaker if the water is too shallow.
Wipe the Whirl-Pak bag with bleach before placing it in the cool bag.
Ensure a field blank is carried in the same cool bag.
Transport samples back for filtration and filter within 24 hours of collection.

steps.title: Filter Water Samples
steps.instruction: Filter water samples using vacuum filtration to capture DNA on filter paper.

substeps.instruction: Set up manifold vacuum filtration equipment, ensuring sides are wiped with bleach and ethanol.
Place a Whatmann filter on the pad.
Pour 500ml of sample into the cup and run for 20 minutes; add more sample if the initial volume filters through within this time.
Tip away any unfiltered sample after 20 minutes.
Run the vacuum pump for an additional 10 seconds to dry the filter.
Remove the cup and roll up the filter paper using sterile tweezers.
Place the filter in a prepared 5ml sterile screw-cap tube containing 1 g each of two garnet bead sizes.
Repeat the filtration process (steps 4.1 and 4.2) for a second 20-minute run and insert the second filter (rolled tighter) into the same screw-cap tube.
Store samples at -20°C for transport and future processing.

steps.title: Collect Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Collect representative soil samples using a quadrat method.

substeps.instruction: Use QGIS tools to generate random sampling points stratified across habitat types.
Set up a 1m² quadrat using a tape measure at the sampling point.
Using a sterile collection spoon and sterile gloves, collect four subsamples (12.5 ml each) from the top 5–10 cm of soil at the four corners of the quadrat.
Combine the four subsamples into a single 50 ml sterile Falcon tube.
Keep used spoons separate from sterile spoons (e.g., in a different cool bag compartment).
Freeze samples at -20°C within a few hours of collection.

steps.title: Collect Tree Roller Samples
steps.instruction: Collect DNA from tree trunks and branches using rollers.

substeps.instruction: Attach a roller to a sterilized frame and extendable pole.
Spray the roller with distilled water to facilitate DNA transfer (unless stored wet).
Roll up and down tree trunks and large branches from ground level up to 3 m for 30 seconds with moderate force.
Place the used roller into a sterile ziploc bag.
Wipe the roller frame and pole with 10% bleach and 70% ethanol between samples.
Create a field blank daily by attaching a roller to the frame and placing it directly into a ziploc bag without touching trees.

steps.title: Process Tree Roller Samples
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from tree rollers via soaking and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Add 300ml of distilled water to the ziploc bag containing the roller.
Massage the roller in the bag to release surface DNA and debris and let soak for 10 minutes.
Squeeze the roller through a modified, tight-fitting pipe within the ziploc bag to remove as much water as possible.
Remove the roller from the bag.
Vacuum-filter the recovered water following the water sample protocol, but using only one filter.
Store samples at -20°C for transport and future processing.

steps.title: Collect Scat Samples
steps.instruction: Opportunistically collect scat samples during fieldwork.

substeps.instruction: Use a sterile spoon to collect the whole scat or a portion that fits within a 50ml Falcon tube.
Freeze samples at -20°C within a few hours of collection.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Perform DNA extraction based on the Mu-DNA workflow.

substeps.instruction: For water samples: Extract both filters together in one extraction; elute in 100 μL of elution buffer.
For tree roller samples: Elute into 50 μL of elution buffer.
For soil and scat samples: Follow the Mu-DNA soil protocol.
Include one extraction blank per batch using the corresponding amount of elution buffer.

steps.title: Perform Post-Extraction Quality Check
steps.instruction: Assess the quality and concentration of extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Use a Nanodrop 1000 Spectrophotometer to measure DNA concentration (ng/μL) and purity ratios (260/280, 260/230).
Store DNA extracts at -20°C until PCR amplification.

steps.title: Construct Sub-libraries (PCR1)
steps.instruction: Perform the first round of PCR to create tagged sub-libraries.

substeps.instruction: Treat groups of up to 24 samples and controls as a sub-library, tagging each with one of 24 unique MID tags.
Pool PCR1 triplicates based on band intensity visualized on a 2% agarose gel: No/very faint = 20 μL; Faint = 15 μL; Bright = 10 μL; Very bright = 5 μL.
Add 2 μL of PCR positive control and 10 μL of any blanks or controls to each library.
Purify the sub-library using Mag-BIND RxnPure Plus beads for double-size magnetic bead selection: add beads at 0.9× ratio (keep supernatant), then 0.15× ratio (discard supernatant).
Note: 100 µL pooled PCR product yields 25 µL cleaned DNA.
Store purified sub-library DNA at 4°C.

steps.title: Perform PCR2 Indexing
steps.instruction: Add Illumina-compatible adapters and dual-indexing tags via a second PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare duplicate 50 µL PCR2 reactions per sub-library containing: 25 µL Q5 Master Mix, 13 µL molecular-grade water, 3 µL of each 10 µM Illumina-indexed primer, and 4 µL cleaned template DNA.
Run PCR2 with cycling conditions: 95°C for 3 min; 10 cycles of 98°C (20s) and 72°C (1 min); final extension at 72°C for 5 min; hold at 4°C.
Pool duplicates and purify using double-size selection with 50 µL of PCR product: add beads at 0.7× ratio (keep supernatant), then 0.15× ratio (discard supernatant).
Elute and store at 4°C.

steps.title: Quantify and Pool Libraries
steps.instruction: Quantify sub-libraries and create final pooled libraries.

substeps.instruction: Quantify each sub-library using a Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer with the dsDNA HS Assay Kit.
Pool sub-libraries proportionally based on the number of samples and DNA concentration.
Create two pooled libraries at 4 nM and 6 nM final concentrations.
Quantify the final pool using the NEBNext Library Quant Kit via qPCR.
Adjust the final library concentration to 4 nM.

steps.title: Sequence on Illumina MiSeq
steps.instruction: Prepare and load the library for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Denature and dilute the final library to 13 pM.
Spike in 10% PhiX Control v3.
Load the library on the Illumina MiSeq using V3 2 × 300 bp chemistry.

steps.title: Filter and Cluster Sequences
steps.instruction: Process raw sequencing data to remove noise and duplicates.

substeps.instruction: Trim adapters and low-quality regions using fastp (5 bp sliding window, min Phred score Q30 across ≥60% of each read).
Remove the first 18 bp of both forward and reverse reads to eliminate primers.
Apply length filtering to retain reads between 90–110 bp.
Merge paired-end reads using fastp (min 20 bp overlap, ≤5% mismatches, ≤5 total mismatched bases).
Retain only forward reads from unmerged pairs.
Remove exact duplicate sequences using VSEARCH with --derep_fulllength.
Discard clusters represented by fewer than three reads.
Perform denoising using VSEARCH with --cluster_unoise, followed by chimera detection using --uchime3_denovo.

steps.title: Assign Taxonomy
steps.instruction: Assign taxonomic identities to the filtered sequences using BLAST+.

substeps.instruction: Compare filtered query sequences against the reference database using BLAST+.
Use a Majority Lowest Common Ancestor (MLCA) approach: retain hits with ≥90% query coverage and ≥98% identity.
Select the top 2% of hits by bit-score.
Require ≥80% of unique taxonomic lineages to agree at a given taxonomic level for assignment.
If only one BLAST hit meets the criteria, assign taxonomy directly to that hit.
Record read counts based on cluster sizes.
Classify sequences that cannot be assigned below order as unassigned.

steps.title: Apply Contamination Thresholds
steps.instruction: Filter results based on the limit of detection (LOD) and read thresholds.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the LOD per species and sample type using species read counts detected in field, extraction, PCR negatives, and positives.
Set any read count below the species-specific LOD to zero.
Apply a 0.1% read threshold, removing any taxonomic assignment comprising less than 0.1% of the total reads in a sample.
